collectionPeriods.description: Collection periods define how often the monitoring system collects metrics (temperature, traffic, energy, etc.) from assets. Each period is expressed by a cron expression, e.g. "every 5 minutes" or "every hour". Agents use these periods to determine how frequently data is collected from each asset.

schedules.description: Monitoring schedules define when the system performs monitoring. "Always (24/7)" means data collection is active at all times; "Scheduled" limits collection to the days and time range you set (e.g. weekdays 08:00–18:00). In agent definitions, one of these schedules is selected to determine when the relevant assets are monitored.

engines.description: Engines are the running services that collect monitoring data and send it to MngReactor or the data gateway. For each engine you define credentials (username/password), status (active, inactive, maintenance), and a "Send schedule" cron that controls how often collected data is sent. Agents connect to a specific engine.

reference.pageSubtitle: Which logs we collect, what they mean in the system, and default alarm scenarios.
reference.intro: This page summarizes how MonitraNG interprets security logs. Collection (NxLog, rsyslog, firewall syslog) is configured in your network; the tables below show supported product scope.
reference.readOnlyTitle: Why can't this page be edited?
reference.readOnlyLead: Log interpretation (parsers) ships with product updates — similar to an antivirus signature pack. Because a wrong mapping can break alarms for everyone, it is not editable from the customer UI.
reference.readOnlyReason1: The same log line must be interpreted reliably and tested in every environment.
reference.readOnlyReason2: Ad-hoc regex or free-form rules risk false alarms or missed detections.
reference.readOnlyReason3: New devices or log formats are added via MonitraNG releases or your support channel.
reference.readOnlyContact: Contact your support team for a new log type or firewall model; this guide is updated when scope changes.
reference.youCanEditAlarms: Alarm thresholds, enable/disable, and additional rules
reference.youCanEditCollectorsHint: Which servers send logs is configured in your infrastructure.
reference.youCanEditSearchHint: Filters and detail on the Security events screen.
reference.weProvideBody: Reading supported log types, normalizing them into common event fields, and default threat scenarios (U1–U7 package). Monitoring (CPU, disk, asset polling) is a separate module; this guide covers security logs only.
reference.collectionSectionHint: Servers and devices push logs to MonitraNG Engine; no asset registry or stored passwords required.
reference.parsersSectionHint: Left column is the source signal; middle column is the short name in the system. Unknown lines are kept raw; default alarms may not fire.
reference.scenariosSectionHint: Default alarm rules can be loaded for U1–U7. U8–U10 events are collected; default package rules are not available yet.
reference.scenariosFootnote: Default alarm package: {id} version {version}. You can change thresholds in Alarm Center.
